# Design rules

The token layer is not a palette with opinions attached. Most of what follows is
enforced by a test, and the ones that are not have a symptom described so they can
be recognised.

## The layers

**Primitives**, five seed colours and a warm neutral ramp generated by holding
cream's hue and decaying chroma toward the dark end, so a grey beside the brand
cream never reads cold. Never referenced directly, and never hand-edited: the ramp
is generated and machine-checked by a round-trip test.

**Semantic tokens**, the names components consume. Each resolves per theme, and
each is either contrast-gated or carries a recorded exemption.

**Scales**, radii, durations, easings, z-index. Named because these are the values
most often re-invented at a call site.

## The vocabulary

Two spellings reach the same runtime variables: the VeloBits names, and shadcn's,
bridged in one `@theme inline` block so light and dark work for free. `bg-panel`
and `bg-card` are the same colour, and existing shadcn components need no
rewriting.

| Role                     | Utility                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Page                     | `bg-bg` (`bg-background`)                                                                                   |
| Secondary fill, wells    | `bg-bg2` (`bg-muted`, `bg-secondary`)                                                                       |
| Panel, card              | `bg-panel` (`bg-card`, `bg-popover`)                                                                        |
| Raised above a panel     | `bg-elevated`                                                                                               |
| Body text                | `text-fg` (`text-foreground`)                                                                               |
| Secondary text           | `text-muted-foreground`, and `text-muted-on-glass` over glass                                               |
| Link                     | `text-link`                                                                                                 |
| Blue fill                | `bg-primary` with `text-primary-foreground`, hover `bg-primary-hover`                                       |
| Blue wash                | `bg-primary-soft`                                                                                           |
| Brand fill               | `bg-brand` with `text-on-brand`, hover `bg-brand-hover`                                                     |
| Brand wash               | `bg-brand-soft`                                                                                             |
| Accent text              | `text-accent-text`                                                                                          |
| Edges                    | `border-border`, controls `border-field-border` (`border-input`)                                            |
| Hover surface            | `bg-highlight` (`bg-accent`)                                                                                |
| Focus ring               | `ring-ring`, and the global `:focus-visible` outline already uses it                                        |
| Scrim behind an overlay  | `bg-overlay`                                                                                                |
| Terminal, code           | `bg-code` with `text-on-code`                                                                               |
| Status fills and washes  | `success`, `danger`, `warning`, `info`, each with a `-soft` wash                                            |
| Text on a danger fill    | `text-on-danger`, hover `bg-danger-hover`                                                                   |
| Categorical, no severity | `rose`, `rose-soft`                                                                                         |
| Chart series             | `chart-1` through `chart-5`                                                                                 |
| Radii                    | `rounded-sm` 4px, `md` 6px, `lg` 10px, `xl` 14px, `2xl` 20px, `pill`                                        |
| Durations                | `duration-micro` 120ms, `duration-enter` 180ms, `duration-overlay` 240ms, `duration-page` 320ms             |
| Easings                  | `ease-out`, `ease-in`, which replace Tailwind's built-ins                                                   |
| Layers                   | `z-base`, `z-raised`, `z-sticky`, `z-dropdown`, `z-overlay`, `z-modal`, `z-popover`, `z-toast`, `z-tooltip` |

Controls use `rounded-md`, app cards `rounded-lg`, marketing cards `rounded-2xl`.

Portalled Radix content lands at `z-dropdown` and above, so sticky app chrome stays
below it. A topbar at a higher layer swallows its own dropdown.

`--color-*` is the bridged spelling and belongs only inside `@theme`. A base-layer
rule must reference the raw variable, `var(--border)` and never
`var(--color-border)`: a `@theme` variable is emitted as a real `:root`
declaration, so the bridged form resolves to the light value once and then inherits
everywhere, and `body.dark` never reaches it. The symptom is a bare `border`
painting light grey in dark mode while `border-border` is correct.

## Three rules the palette encodes

**`--primary` is not a text colour.** `#007ACC` measures 3.86:1 on the paper page:
fine as a fill behind white text at 4.51:1, a WCAG failure as text. Links use
`text-link`, no `Button` variant paints primary as a foreground, and a test enforces
that.

**Lime is asymmetric.** `bg-brand` with `text-on-brand` (charcoal) is 10.89:1 and is
the only sanctioned pairing; white on lime is 1.31:1. Lime **as text** is 13.9:1 in
dark and 1.13:1 in light, so `--accent-text` is lime in dark and plum in light,
which is one token doing one job in each theme rather than two hats. A lime fill also
cannot be the lone graphical indicator in light mode.

**Glass is a tier, not a decoration.** See below.

## The two glass tiers

| Tier                      | Class                                   | For                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Tier O, overlay           | `.glass`, `.glass-elevated`             | Surfaces floating over arbitrary content: Dialog, SidePanel, Popover, DropdownMenu, Toast, CommandPalette, sticky headers |
| Tier S, component surface | `.glass-surface`, `.glass-surface-blur` | Surfaces whose backdrop is known to be the page: Card, Alert, and the Table, Accordion and EmptyState shells              |

Tier S carries **no `backdrop-filter`** by default, so a 20-card grid does not mount
20 blur layers. `.glass-surface-blur` is the opt-in for the rare case that wants one.

Forbidden on both: page backgrounds, rows inside a scroll container, anything that
repaints on scroll, and **nested glass**, where two instances of one tier composite
about 2/255 apart and cancel each other out.

Reach for a component's `surface` prop rather than a `bg-*` utility. Every
surface-bearing component has one, and a utility wins the cascade and takes the
material with it.

`.control-raised` and `.control-recessed` are the same language applied to controls,
which is why a Card no longer reads as glass with paper inside it. `.page-texture` is
opt-in per element and never on `body`.

## The contrast gate

Every semantic pair is asserted against its WCAG target in both themes, and every
Tier-O glass tier against the seven worst-case backdrops in the palette, composited
in **gamma-encoded sRGB**, because that is what browsers do. Measuring in linear
light overstates glass legibility by a wide margin.

Three registries carry it:

- **Flat pairs**, a token against a token.
- **Soft-chip pairs**, each composited over the page, the panel and the Tier-S glass
  composite, in both themes. A chip is never seen against the colour it is declared
  with, which a flat pair cannot express.
- **Perceptibility pairs**, every tier must clear 8/255 max-channel distance from what
  it sits on. Translucency is worthless if the result is the colour underneath, and
  this is the gate that caught a dark overlay compositing byte-identical with the page.

**Changing a colour means measuring it.** Override a token after the import, in both
themes or the one you mean:

```css
@import '@velobitsio/tokens/theme.css';

:root {
  --primary: #0a6ebd;
}
.dark {
  --primary: #4aa3e0;
}
```

Then check the pairs it appears in. `https://ui.velobits.dev/docs/colors` renders all
three registries live, computed by the same functions the CI gate uses. A colour
change that skips this is a contrast regression with a green build in the consuming
app, because the gate lives here.

## Accessibility, the parts that are load-bearing

- **Colour is never the only signal.** Every status in `StatusChip` ships a distinct
  glyph, because colour alone fails 1.4.1 and on-versus-off is the distinction a
  control plane exists to make unambiguous. Chart series are isoluminant and separated
  by hue, so a chart also needs shape, pattern or a direct label.
- **One focus ring for the system**, `:focus-visible` with an `outline` rather than a
  `box-shadow`, so an ancestor's `overflow: hidden` cannot clip it. Do not replace it
  per component.
- **Scroll containers must be reachable by keyboard.** A `pre` that scrolls carries
  `tabIndex={0}` for 2.1.1; the same applies to any hand-rolled scroll region.
- Structural a11y on every primitive is asserted with axe in `packages/ui`. Contrast
  rules are deliberately disabled there, happy-dom has no cascade, and the token suite
  measures the values directly instead.

## Motion

Reduced motion is handled in exactly two places, and adding a third is how they get
out of step. `VelobitsProvider` mounts `<MotionConfig reducedMotion="user">`, which
drops transform and opacity animations for users who asked for less motion across
every component without any of them knowing. The token layer's
`@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block clamps CSS durations globally.

`usePrefersReducedMotion()` is for imperative decisions neither of those can see,
such as whether to autoplay something. Not for animations.

Use the named durations. `duration-enter` for something appearing, `duration-overlay`
for an overlay, `duration-page` for a route transition, `duration-micro` for a state
flip on a control.

## Dark mode

Class-based: `.dark` on the toggled element swaps every semantic token. The variant
matches the element itself as well as its descendants, so `html.dark` and `body.dark`
both work, which is why the Keycloak theme can toggle the one the editor and
dashboard apps do not.

Both themes are first-class. Dark is not a filter over light, and several tokens are
not the same colour scaled: `--accent-text` swaps hue, and `--on-danger` is white in
light and charcoal in dark because dark's danger fill is a light red that also has to
work as text.

The hydration trap and the `mounted` escape hatch are in `SKILL.md`, section 5.

## Fonts

The token layer names the typefaces and deliberately does not ship them, so the
package stays dependency-free. `--font-sans` is Geist, `--font-mono` is JetBrains
Mono, `--font-display-marketing` is Syne and is website-only.

Skipping the faces fails quietly: everything falls back to `system-ui`, the layout
barely shifts, and the only visible symptom is a glyph the fallback lacks rendering
as tofu. The `⌘` in `Kbd` is what gave it away here.

## Tailwind v4 specifics that bite

- **`z-*` and `duration-*` are `@utility` rules, not theme values.** Tailwind v4 has
  no `--z-index-*` or `--duration-*` namespace, so declaring them in `@theme` emits a
  variable and no utility, and `z-tooltip` would silently do nothing. They are real
  utilities in the token layer; do not redeclare them.
- **Renaming a `@theme` token needs a dev-server restart.** Tailwind's candidate cache
  lies through HMR.
- **Custom scale values need registering with `tailwind-merge`**, which is why our `cn`
  is a superset. It cannot resolve a conflict it does not recognise, so `rounded-pill`
  left `rounded-md` in place and stylesheet order decided the winner.
- **v4 dropped Preflight's default border colour**, so `border` emits width and style
  only and the colour falls back to `currentColor`. The token layer's base reset sets
  it; an app that resets borders itself must keep that rule.
